units.function: CLI tests for login option registration and challenge create/get/approve/cancel plus current-token revocation route parity.
units.dependencyDirection: Imports auth CLI registration and mocks fetch; it does not invoke challenge services, browser callback handling, identity verification or audit persistence.
units.keyDataModels: Company option, no-browser flag, challenge ID, challenge Secret from argument/environment and board API key.
units.lifecycle: Registers commands, creates/reads/approves/cancels a challenge, approves an encoded ID with env Secret and revokes the current credential.
units.testAssessment: Three tests passed. Option/route wiring and encoded IDs are covered, but browser fallback, token headers/redaction, expiry, replay, state/PKCE, approver authority, tenant denial, stable errors and real effects are absent.
units.designRationale: Offer interactive and headless CLI authentication with challenge approval and an operator escape hatch when a browser cannot open.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs secure device/CLI authorization that binds a human identity and explicit company scope without leaking bearer material.
units.companyOsFit: REJECT this test contract because it normalizes a challenge Secret in a GET query. Rebuild around short-lived single-use device codes or authorization code plus PKCE, Secret-free URLs/logs, explicit audience/company binding, revocation and accountable approval evidence; retain only no-browser UX and encoded-ID test ideas.
units.responsibilityConflict: Challenge approval is reduced to an unaudited POST with a static board token; the suite cannot prove who approved, their company authority, exact requested grant, expiry or resulting credential audience.
evidence: 2026-08-18 focused Vitest: 3 passed in combined 6-test run

units.function: Filesystem tests for board credential store creation defaults, API-base-keyed retrieval and removal.
units.dependencyDirection: Calls production credential-store helpers against temporary files; it does not invoke server auth, OS keychain or token validation.
units.keyDataModels: Versioned credential map keyed by normalized API base, bearer token and optional user ID.
units.lifecycle: Reads an absent store, writes/retrieves one credential and removes it.
units.testAssessment: Three tests passed. Basic normalization and lifecycle work, but permissions, encrypted/keychain storage, atomicity, symlinks, corruption/concurrency, token expiry/rotation, origin canonicalization and fixture cleanup are untested.
units.designRationale: Allow a CLI to remember separate board credentials for multiple server origins.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS operator tooling needs per-deployment credentials with strong origin/audience isolation and secure local storage.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE ONLY for the versioned per-origin store shape. Prefer OS credential storage or a pluggable SecretStore, enforce HTTPS/origin canonicalization, store metadata rather than raw long-lived tokens when possible, and test permissions, rotation, corruption, concurrency and cleanup.
units.responsibilityConflict: A locally retrievable bearer token identifies possession, not accountable human intent for each high-risk action; responsibility evidence must be created at action approval/execution boundaries.
evidence: 2026-08-18 focused Vitest: 3 passed in combined 6-test run
